solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Play wind instrument, perhaps: a dangerous weapon!

parts.note: to play a horn or whistle is to blow it
a pipe is one example of a wind instrument, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A musician is warned that blowing into some instruments can turn deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads like an instruction to a musician; split it as two words and they join into the name of a tube that shoots darts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube through which poisoned darts are puffed is a hunting and fighting weapon.

definitions.meaning: a horse that leaps with arched back trying to throw its rider is said to do this
a male antelope or deer is given this name

explanation.surface: A leap made by either a horse or an antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco's rearing leap and a male deer or antelope share the same word.

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
to set a question is to pose it, so set means posed

explanation.surface: Someone objects to work that has been set.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hostile or in opposition to something means being against it.

clue.text: Before records were made, priest and choir worked together

indicators.note: worked together suggests the letters of the two words are kneaded and mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: In ancient times a cleric and his singers collaborated.
explanation.definitionFit: The era before written history began is described this way.

clue.text: Proposals to tour one flat country

indicators.note: to tour is to go around, so the proposals word wraps around the numeral

parts.note: plans are proposals
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Plans for a single trip around a level land.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide areas of level, treeless land are flat country.

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for impertinence is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: gall is cheeky boldness or nerve

explanation.surface: Someone is struck by the cheek of an ancient tribesman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gauls were Celtic tribes of ancient France, so one of them is an old tribesman.

parts.note: a bout is a boxing or wrestling contest

explanation.surface: A fight that is not quite a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Approximately, roughly, or around a figure means not exactly.

definitions.meaning: a thinking pause, said while considering an answer
a request to be allowed to look

explanation.surface: Someone muses aloud while asking another to stop standing in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as a stalling filler while thinking and as asking for a look.

parts.note: cops is slang for police officers

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word leave

explanation.surface: Officers at last withdraw from a little woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A thicket or small group of trees is a little wood.

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
the face of a building is its front

explanation.surface: An insult delivered with a fine bold face.
explanation.definitionFit: To insult someone openly is to show them disrespect; both serve as verb and noun.

clue.text: After lunch, vegetarian may be in high spirits

definitions.meaning: a vegetarian who has eaten pulses at lunch is stuffed with them, read literally

explanation.surface: A vegetarian feels lively after eating lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means bursting with energy and enthusiasm, while literally it describes a stomach of pulses.

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so the letters of the two words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A customer earnestly asks a barista to make some coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky espresso drink made with skimmed milk is a kind of coffee.

indicators.note: Not means the letter named by the following word is left out

parts.note: a suppliant is one who humbly petitions

explanation.surface: A petitioner asks whether they are being replaced and is told no.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust and take the place of another is to replace them.

clue.text: Brief appointment — out of bed first

indicators.note: first tells us the out-of-bed word is placed before the appointment word

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: A short meeting, but get up beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective describing the appointment, but it is the verb meaning to inform.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to give them the latest information, bringing them current.

clue.text: Depart to stare at popular website

parts.note: to depart is to go
to ogle is to stare at, usually lecherously

explanation.surface: Leave so you can gawp at a website everyone uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The search engine is among the most visited sites on the internet.

parts.note: got means received
the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An obituary: he retired, was honoured, then died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retire' reads as stopping work, but here it means turning in for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire at night is to head off to sleep.

clue.text: American prison is over that ravine

indicators.note: in a down clue the prison word sits above the word for that

parts.note: the can is US slang for jail
yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in yonder

explanation.surface: An American jail stands beyond that gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, narrow gorge cut by a river is a ravine.

clue.text: Potter's creation safe, teacher felt finally

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word felt

explanation.surface: A potter's work involving a safe and a teacher's final feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' is Beatrix Potter, the children's author, not a maker of pots; peter for a safe is old thieves' slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix Potter wrote and illustrated tales of a mischievous bunny in a blue jacket.

clue.text: Follow behind, right in the rear

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation is placed inside the rear word

parts.note: the tail is the rear end

explanation.surface: Following along, staying at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag along after someone or track them is to follow behind.

indicators.note: an eddy swirls about, and swirling stirs the letters of the word into a new order

explanation.surface: A whirlpool with oddly bright colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or fabric coloured artificially has been tinted with a pigment, so is not naturally coloured.

indicators.note: in tells us the expert word sits inside the word for some

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'
arch means cunning or knowing, hence expert

explanation.surface: A specialist in a certain kind of disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawlessness and total disorder, with no government, is chaos.

parts.note: by a place is at it
a bay is an inlet of the sea

explanation.surface: Someone trapped beside a small inlet of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunted animal held at bay is trapped and forced to turn and face its pursuers.

indicators.note: back means those letters are read in reverse order
in shows the letters sit inside the word allotment

explanation.surface: A ring turns up when digging in the allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a rented plot of land for growing vegetables in Britain. 'in' finds LLOT inside it and 'back' turns those letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring a bell slowly, as for a funeral, is to toll it.

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are prejudiced and gets a blunt yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A partial or unfair view favours only one party, which is being biased.
